article.title: Unraveling the Evolution of an Unusually Active Earthquake Sequence Near Sheldon, Nevada
article.scientific_question: Characterize the unusual Sheldon, Nevada earthquake sequence using routine locations, high-precision relocations, machine-learning detections, moment tensors, and source spectra.
article.sequence: Sheldon Wildlife Refuge, northwest Nevada; sequence began July 2014 and remained highly active through 2016 (paper also describes a longer 40-month detection record).
article.catalog_relationship: Real catalog-construction research, but not a Yellowstone Maple Creek source. It is retained only as out-of-case context and must not supply Maple event labels or counts.

evidence.note: Article identity, Sheldon location, purpose, and approximate detection/located-event statistics.
Local reading explicitly classifies the article as Sheldon/Nevada context-only for the Maple case.

catalog.name: Sheldon Nevada sequence products (out-of-case context)
catalog.scientific_purpose: Context for how a sparse-network sequence can combine routine locations, relative relocation, and single-station ML detection; not a Yellowstone benchmark reference.
catalog.event_definition: Article describes several distinct populations: routinely located NSL/ComCat events, a GrowClust-relocated M_L >= 1 subset, and COLR single-station machine-learning detections.

product_semantics.routine_locations: Analyst-reviewed NSL/ComCat origins; article reports 7,966 located events.
product_semantics.growclust_subset: Relative relocation subset; article reports 3,811 of 6,533 M_L >= 1 events.
product_semantics.colr_detections: Single-station EQ-Transformer detections at COLR; article reports nearly 70,000 detections over the high-activity record.
product_semantics.moment_tensor_subset: Quality-controlled moment-tensor solutions; article reports 93 with variance reduction >40%.

construction_workflow.summary: For Sheldon (not Maple), the article combines NSL/ComCat analyst phase arrivals and waveforms, NonLinLoc absolute locations, GrowClust3D differential-time relative relocation, and COLR EQ-Transformer single-station detections; moment tensors and source spectra are additional products.

input_data.name: NSL/partner network phase arrivals, origins, and waveforms
input_data.provider_or_network: Nevada Seismological Laboratory and partner networks NC, BK, UO, UW
input_data.temporal_spatial_scope: Sheldon sequence, stations within 250 km for routine products
input_data.availability_conditions: Sparse regional coverage; temporary COLR station installed 2014-11-18 and operated through 2018-02-06.

evidence.note: Input database, partner networks, 250 km extraction, and COLR deployment.

input_data.name: COLR continuous three-component waveforms
input_data.temporal_spatial_scope: November 2014–February 2016 detection interval; station operated through 2018-02-06
input_data.channels_sampling: Three-component broadband/strong-motion; exact sample rate not extracted
input_data.availability_conditions: Reliable cellular communications and high signal quality near the sequence.

evidence.note: COLR waveform period and single-station detection input.

input_data.name: 1-D velocity model and station corrections
input_data.availability_conditions: Used for NonLinLoc and GrowClust3D station-specific travel-time grids.

evidence.note: NonLinLoc correction and GrowClust3D travel-time grids.

stages.name: Routine absolute locations
stages.purpose: Estimate absolute origins from analyst phase arrivals.
stages.method: NonLinLoc with an initial station-phase correction run followed by a corrected run.
stages.analyst_intervention: Analyst-reviewed phase arrivals are the starting bulletin.
stages.dependencies: S3 velocity model and station corrections.

stages.name: Relative relocation
stages.purpose: Refine locations using waveform differential times.
stages.method: Pair events within 5 km; cross-correlate P/S windows; retain correlation >=0.65 and at least 8 qualifying differential times per pair.
qc_and_rejection_rules: Discard cross-correlation measurements with peak sidelobe within 0.10 amplitude units of the peak.
stages.analyst_intervention: The article specifies analyst arrivals and quality-control thresholds.
stages.dependencies: S1 waveforms/phases and S3 travel-time grids.

stages.name: Single-station ML detection
stages.purpose: Recover small events below the regional-network location threshold.
outputs: COLR detection population and single-station M_L estimates
stages.method: EQ-Transformer phase detection, duplicate/low-SNR filtering, temporal association, and Wood-Anderson amplitude magnitude estimate.

parameters.name: distance_assumption
parameters.note: Approximate source-to-COLR distance for M_L correction.

qc_and_rejection_rules: Remove duplicate arrivals and unusually low-SNR arrivals; associate by temporal clustering and short S–P time.
stages.intermediate_result: Nearly 70,000 detections reported; approximate count, not locally audited.
stages.analyst_intervention: The article describes a source-locality assumption for arrivals not seen at distant stations.
stages.dependencies: COLR continuity and sparse regional background.

evidence.note: Model, filtering, association, and magnitude method.

construction_workflow.final_output: Multiple Sheldon products (routine locations, GrowClust3D subset, COLR detections, moment tensors, and source spectra) archived by the article; none are a Maple Creek release in this repository.

scientific_findings.statement: The Sheldon sequence is characterized by an east-dipping normal fault intersecting a secondary subvertical cross fault.
Sparse station coverage motivated a separate COLR single-station detection product below the routine network threshold.
